Reference for import praisonaiui as aiui.
These functions configure the server. Call them at module level in your app.py, before the server starts.

Set the UI style. Parameter Type Values style str "app" (the React app shell), "chat" (the classic chat), "dashboard", "agents", "playground", "docs", "custom" Priority under aiui run: CLI --style, then set_style(), then auto-detection (a plain chat app gets app). See UI Styles.

Choose which pages the app shows besides its own, in every style. The list covers built-in pages, the app shell's layout pages (start, artifacts, templates, connect, api-reference, ...) and dashboard-plugin folders, including the ones in ~/.praisonai/dashboard-plugins that every app on the machine would otherwise share. Pages the app registers itself (@aiui.page(), register_page, register_plugin) and installed entry-point plugins always appear. Without set_pages every page shows. An id that names no page is reported with a warning at startup. Use aiui pages ids to see all available page IDs, or inspect aiui.PAGE_PRESETS for the built-in preset definitions (minimal, agent, ops). aiui.set_pages("all") / aiui.set_pages("ops") (or aiui run app.py --preset ops / --pages all) shows every page and makes every layout's sidebar list them all, grouped (Agent, Work, Control, ...), as the legacy dashboard did: each page in its React version where there is one, otherwise the legacy view inside the app shell. The layout picker keeps working. aiui run --pages chat,sessions is the same as set_pages(["chat", "sessions"]). The app's own pages (register_page, @aiui.page) are listed in their group in every layout's sidebar, not only under More (⌘K).
Shorthand for set_pages(list(keep)): aiui.only_my_pages() shows only the app's own pages, aiui.only_my_pages("chat") adds Chat.

Build a minimal Starlette ASGI app that mounts only the React app shell, selected pages, plugin assets/routes, and caller-supplied routes — without mounting agent server endpoints (/sessions, /run, /agents, /teams, /api/chat/*) or the 48 backend agent features (unmatched paths return 404). Pass csp="strict" (a directive dict, or (html, hashes) -> str) to attach a strict Content-Security-Policy header with exact 'sha256-…' hashes for the shell's executable inline scripts. Related helpers: aiui.render_shell_html(request=None, *, style="app") → (html, inline_script_hashes) aiui.shell_inline_script_hashes(html) → sorted 'sha256-…' tuple (skips type="application/json" and src="…") aiui.shell_csp_header(html, *, base=None, extra=None) → rendered Content-Security-Policy header value See Build a focused app → Mount only the shell.

Pause the agent and wait for the user to answer. Preferred entry point for interactive agent flows — supersedes the legacy AskUserMessage class. Parameter Type Description question str Text shown to the user. options list[str] \ None Optional list of choices. When given, the user picks one; otherwise they type free text. timeout float Seconds to wait before giving up. Default 300 (5 min). Returns a PromptResult dataclass (text, choice, message_id). The result is truthy when the user answered, falsy on timeout. The answer comes back over the chat WebSocket (ask_response), so a question needs the WebSocket transport; the HTTP fallback (POST /run) can show it but not answer it. Time spent waiting for the answer does not count against the @reply inactivity timeout (AIUI_REPLY_IDLE_TIMEOUT). aiui.ask and AskUserMessage work the same way.
Emit an error message to the chat. A thin helper around Message with metadata={"kind": "error"} — keeps the public surface small.

One call for the common setters. Every keyword is optional; each one is forwarded to the matching set_* function, which you can still call directly. Parameter Type Description datastore str Storage backend: "memory", "json", "json:/path", "sdk", "sdk:/path". branding dict Forwarded to set_branding(...). Keys: title, logo (any other key raises TypeError). theme dict Forwarded to set_theme(...). Keys: preset, dark/dark_mode, radius; brand_color goes to set_brand_color(). chat dict feedback goes to set_feedback_enabled(), mode to set_chat_mode(), other keys to set_chat_features(). custom_css str CSS text, passed to set_custom_css() unchanged. It is not read from a file: pass Path("styles.css").read_text() to use one. custom_js str \ Path Path to a JS file; same as set_custom_js. style str UI style — "chat", "dashboard", etc.

Handle incoming chat messages. This is the core callback. Annotate the parameter as str (async def on_reply(message: str)) to get the text only. Otherwise the callback gets a MessageContext with: message.text (alias message.content): the user's text message.session_id: the session id message.agent_name: the selected agent, if any message.attachments: the files sent with the message, [{id, name, content_type, path}] (see Attachments) How a reply ends: If the callback raises, the run ends with one run_error frame carrying the exception text. The chat shows the error under whatever was streamed, the reply is saved with status: "error" (so it is still there after a reload), the run ledger counts it as failed, and the traceback is logged. Stop (chat_abort, POST /api/chat/abort, POST /cancel) cancels the callback task: the callback gets asyncio.CancelledError at its next await, so an LLM call or tool it is waiting on stops too. A callback that sends nothing (no token, message, step or tool event) for AIUI_REPLY_IDLE_TIMEOUT seconds (default 600) is cancelled and the run fails with a timeout. Set AIUI_REPLY_IDLE_TIMEOUT=0 for no limit.

The greeting on a new, empty chat. The chat runs it through POST /welcome once per page load and shows what it says (aiui.say, or streamed tokens) as plain text on the empty thread: in the app shell's chat and every layout, the chat style and the dashboard's chat. In a layout's new-chat hero (the site's mark and name) the greeting takes the place of the generic "Ask anything…" line, with the starters below it. It is not saved to the conversation. A chat YAML's welcome: key registers one for you.

Runs when a chat's last browser connection closes, after any reply still running there finishes, as that chat (aiui.user_session is readable): use it for clean-up. Nobody is listening any more, so what it sends is dropped.

Each moment of a chat has a handler. The names are aliases: @aiui.on_message and @aiui.reply register the same handler (the last one registered wins). Decorator Runs Same as @aiui.on_message For each message the user sends; gets the MessageContext (message.content). @aiui.reply @aiui.on_chat_start Once per chat, right before its first reply (again after on_chat_end ran for it). @aiui.on_stop When the user presses Stop, as the stopped chat. @aiui.cancel @aiui.on_chat_end When the chat ends (above). @aiui.goodbye @aiui.author_rename Maps an author (agent) name to the name the chat shows. @aiui.welcome The greeting on an empty chat, once per page load (no chat yet). Every handler may be async def or a plain def. on_chat_start runs in the reply's task (so aiui.say and aiui.Message work) and needs a reply handler; if it raises, that turn fails with the error and the next turn runs it again. author_rename is called once per name per reply (a failing handler keeps the name); the display name goes on every frame of the reply (agent_name) and the saved reply, never on the agent the user picked. @aiui.resume is not called yet (below).

Register a custom page. The callback's return value is the page data (GET /api/pages/ /data); return aiui.layout([...]) to render UI blocks inside the React app shell (the default). Use @aiui.register_page_action(id) to handle form submissions, editable aiui.sheet(..., action=...) saves, or streaming yield generators (application/x-ndjson). aiui.register_page(id, *, title, ...) registers a page without a decorator.

Register a 5-line Gradio-style interactive page backed by a single Python function (sync, async def, sync generator, or async generator yield). Accepts shorthand input names ("text", "textarea", "number", "checkbox", "file") or full aiui.* input blocks (including aiui.file_upload()). Uploaded files are resolved automatically via aiui.get_uploaded_file() and unverified/forged handles resolve to None.

Resolve an attachment UUID (or handle dict submitted by aiui.file_upload()) to verified server file metadata ({id, filename, content_type, size, path, session_id}), or None if unknown, malformed, or expired. Always use this instead of trusting client-supplied paths.

Control read-only access to shared thread links (GET /shared/{token}). Returns True to allow access, False to deny (default: deny when unregistered). Related helpers: aiui.create_share_token(thread_id, created_by), aiui.get_thread_by_share_token(token), aiui.revoke_share_token(thread_id, user_id), aiui.list_share_tokens(user_id), and aiui.get_share_url(token, base_url=""). See Session Management → Thread Sharing.

Async functions for sending messages to the user. Call inside callback handlers. Function Purpose await aiui.say(content) Send a complete message await aiui.send_block(block, *, name=None, id=None) Render any of the 81 UI blocks, aiui.layout([...]), pandas/Polars DataFrame, or Plotly figure inline inside chat await aiui.stream_token(token) Append a token to the streaming reply await aiui.stream(token) Same as stream_token await aiui.think(step) Show a reasoning step await aiui.ask(question, options=None, timeout=300.0) Ask the user and wait; returns the answer text await aiui.image(url, alt="") Send an image await aiui.audio(url) Send audio await aiui.video(url) Send video await aiui.file(url, name="") Send a file await aiui.action_buttons(buttons) Show buttons; handle clicks with @aiui.button(name) await aiui.tool(name, args=None, result=None) Show a tool call and its result
